## Our model now

On the block drawn on the Qing plan S01: position and frontage from the plan, heights and roof from the typology of its hall class, its form drawn by the hall kit. It will be updated as the research goes on.

- **Box:** 9.6 × 12.1 m, side hall
- **Heights:** platform 0.54 m, eave 3.64 m, ridge 5.9 m above the ground
- **Roof:** gable 硬山 or 悬山, rolled ridge 卷棚, 2 parallel rolls 勾连搭, grey tile
- **Faces:** 175.3° from north
- **Drawn:** by the hall kit: 2 bays, a porch front, steps on the front, left, 硬山 flush gable with a rolled ridge 卷棚, grey tile, a painted beam under the eave. Drawn from the typology of its hall class, not from a picture of this hall (assumed, C).
- **Confidence:** B

## Texts and drawings (2)

- **E0499** (description, sure): 三类 形制, 山墙 红色 (S47 section 3). 2012, citing archive and Qing texts · pp.121-123 · S47. https://www.dpm.org.cn/Uploads/File/2018/06/15/u5b23730ae0e5a.pdf
  S47 sorts the shrines in three types by form and notes that on the album the gable walls of seven of them are painted red, against grey or white on other buildings: 瑞应宫, 太岁坛, the 杏花春馆 earth shrine, the 北远山村 and 涵虚朗鉴 dragon shrines, 广育宫 and 多宝阁. A colour rule usable for the models.
- **E2379** (description, likely): 贾珺 on 北远山村 龙王庙, later 观音庵. 2012 · S47 p.113 and table row 15 · S47. https://www.dpm.org.cn/Uploads/File/2018/06/15/u5b23730ae0e5a.pdf
  North-west of 北远山村: octagonal pyramid-roof hall with a one-bay south porch, built 1733 for Yongzheng's tablet of the rain god, from 1734 a dragon-king temple, later 观音庵, date unknown. The plan's 观音庵 is a round building on a mound just inside the north gate, about 55 m from the listed centre of YM26 (own calculation): it fits form, place and name. S47 fig.7 shows it.

**On the plan:** Drawn on the plan of the gardens (S01), labelled 观音庵. https://artmuseum.princeton.edu/collections/objects/138657
